passages.text: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm.
He wrote it to teach others.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
He said to sing it to the tune called “The Lily of the Covenant.”
David fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah.
Joab was David’s commander.
Joab returned from battle.
Joab struck down 12,000 Edomites.
This happened in the Valley of Salt.

passages.text: You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
passages.sermon:
David wrote this psalm to teach others.
He gave it to the choirmaster.
The psalm uses the tune “The Lily of the Covenant.”
David fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah.
Joab returned after the battle.
Joab struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
God, You have rejected us.
You have broken us.
You have been angry with us.
God, restore us.
passages.original: לַ֭מְנַצֵּחַ עַל־ שׁוּשַׁ֣ן עֵד֑וּת מִכְתָּ֖ם לְדָוִ֣ד לְלַמֵּֽד׃ בְּהַצּוֹת֨וֹ׀ אֶ֥ת אֲרַ֣ם נַהֲרַיִם֮ וְאֶת־ אֲרַ֪ם צ֫וֹבָ֥ה וַיָּ֤שָׁב יוֹאָ֗ב וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־ אֱד֣וֹם בְּגֵיא־ מֶ֑לַח שְׁנֵ֖ים עָשָׂ֣ר אָֽלֶף׃ אֱ֭לֹהִים זְנַחְתָּ֣נוּ פְרַצְתָּ֑נוּ אָ֝נַ֗פְתָּ תְּשׁ֣וֹבֵ֥ב לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.
passages.sermon:
God, You have shaken the land.
You have torn the land open.
The land has many fractures.
The land is quaking.
Heal the land’s fractures.
passages.original: הִרְעַ֣שְׁתָּה אֶ֣רֶץ פְּצַמְתָּ֑הּ רְפָ֖ה שְׁבָרֶ֣יהָ כִי־ מָֽטָה׃

passages.text: You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.
passages.sermon:
God, You have shown hardship to Your people.
You made us experience suffering.
You gave us wine that makes us stagger.
We feel weak and unsteady because of what You gave us.
passages.original: הִרְאִ֣יתָה עַמְּךָ֣ קָשָׁ֑ה הִ֝שְׁקִיתָ֗נוּ יַ֣יִן תַּרְעֵלָֽה׃

passages.text: You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
passages.sermon:
God gives a banner to those who fear Him.
This banner stands high.
God does this so His people can escape danger.
They can flee from the enemy’s bow.
Selah.
God, save us with Your right hand.
Answer us.
Deliver those You love.
passages.original: נָ֘תַ֤תָּה לִּירֵאֶ֣יךָ נֵּ֭ס לְהִתְנוֹסֵ֑ס מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י קֹ֣שֶׁט סֶֽלָה׃ לְ֭מַעַן יֵחָלְצ֣וּן יְדִידֶ֑יךָ הוֹשִׁ֖יעָה יְמִֽינְךָ֣ וַעֲנֵנוּ׃

passages.text: God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
passages.sermon:
God spoke from His holy place.
God said He will have victory.
God will divide Shechem.
God will measure out the Valley of Succoth.
passages.original: אֱלֹהִ֤ים׀ דִּבֶּ֥ר בְּקָדְשׁ֗וֹ אֶ֫עְלֹ֥זָה אֲחַלְּקָ֥ה שְׁכֶ֑ם וְעֵ֖מֶק סֻכּ֣וֹת אֲמַדֵּֽד׃

passages.text: Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority and power.
God claims Gilead as His own.
God claims Manasseh as His own.
God uses Ephraim as His helmet.
God uses Judah as His scepter.
passages.original: לִ֤י גִלְעָ֨ד׀ וְלִ֬י מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה וְ֭אֶפְרַיִם מָע֣וֹז רֹאשִׁ֑י יְ֝הוּדָ֗ה מְחֹֽקְקִי׃

passages.text: Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks with authority and power.
God says, “Moab is My washbasin.
I use Moab for My purposes.
I throw My sandal on Edom.
I show My control over Edom.
I shout in victory over Philistia.
I am triumphant over Philistia.”
passages.original: מוֹאָ֤ב׀ סִ֬יר רַחְצִ֗י עַל־ אֱ֭דוֹם אַשְׁלִ֣יךְ נַעֲלִ֑י עָ֝לַ֗י פְּלֶ֣שֶׁת הִתְרֹעָֽעִֽי׃

passages.text: Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
passages.sermon:
The speaker is asking for a guide.
\r\nThe speaker wants to reach a strong, fortified city.
\r\nThe speaker asks, "Who will bring me to the fortified city?"
\r\nThe speaker also wants to go to Edom.
\r\nThe speaker asks, "Who will lead me to Edom?"
passages.original: מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי עִ֣יר מָצ֑וֹר מִ֖י נָחַ֣נִי עַד־ אֱדֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
passages.sermon: God, You have rejected us.\r\nYou do not go out with our armies.\r\nYou no longer march with us.
passages.original: הֲלֹֽא־ אַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֣ים זְנַחְתָּ֑נוּ וְֽלֹא־ תֵצֵ֥א אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בְּצִבְאוֹתֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
passages.sermon: God, give us help against our enemy.\r\nThe help of people is useless.\r\nOnly You can save us.
passages.original: הָֽבָה־ לָּ֣נוּ עֶזְרָ֣ת מִצָּ֑ר וְ֝שָׁ֗וְא תְּשׁוּעַ֥ת אָדָם׃

passages.text: With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.
passages.sermon:
God gives us strength.
We act bravely with God.
God defeats our enemies.
God tramples those who oppose us.
passages.original: בֵּֽאלֹהִ֥ים נַעֲשֶׂה־ חָ֑יִל וְ֝ה֗וּא יָב֥וּס צָרֵֽינוּ׃
